3
The arrow represents a vector R.
Which diagram does not represent R as two perpendicular components?
A
B
C
D

hints: Look at the original $R$ which points up and to the right with a small slope, and compare its length and direction with the resultant formed in each diagram.
Remember two perpendicular components must satisfy two tests: the angle between them when placed tail to tail is $90^{\circ}$, and their vector sum must equal $R$.
Try joining the two component arrows head to tail in each diagram and see which triangle fails to close with the same length and direction as $R$.
walkthrough: The given vector $R$ points to the right and slightly upward. Any pair of perpendicular components must add by the triangle or parallelogram rule to give exactly this $R$.
The rule is: if the two components are placed tail to tail they must be at $90^{\circ}$, and if placed head to tail the second must start at the head of the first and finish at the head of $R$.
In A, the vertical and horizontal arrows are clearly $90^{\circ}$ apart and form the sides of a rectangle whose diagonal is $R$.
In B and D, the pairs are also at $90^{\circ}$ and can be arranged head to tail to close a right-angled triangle with $R$ as the third side.
In C, the two arrows are at $90^{\circ}$ to each other, but joining them head to tail gives a resultant that is longer than $R$ and points in a different direction.
Therefore C fails the vector-addition test and does not represent $R$ as two perpendicular components. This is option C

A.explanation: The horizontal and vertical arrows are perpendicular and placed tail to tail they form a rectangle with $R$ as the diagonal, so their vector sum is $R$.

B.explanation: The short near-vertical arrow and the long arrow parallel to $R$ are perpendicular, and placed head to tail they close to give $R$.

C.explanation: Although the two arrows are perpendicular, their vector sum placed head to tail is longer and steeper than $R$, so they do not combine to $R$.

D.explanation: The two arrows are perpendicular and placed head to tail they form a right-angled triangle with $R$ as the resultant.
